Under the Second Restatement approach, the plaintiff is required to assert all claims arising out of the transaction in the first action, whether or not the defendant litigated the issues involved in those claims. D is wrong, because the Second Restatement approach does not focus on the legal theory of recovery, but on the underlying transaction. Both actions arise out of the same transaction, the construction of the addition, so the second is barred by res judicata.
